title: Evaluation and validation of p53 expression in oral cavity and laryngeal carcinomas and their precancerous lesions for the purpose of early tumor detection, as well as a predictor of treatment response and the occurrence of recurrence
summary:
Head and neck cancers are among the most common types of cancer worldwide. A major challenge is the early detection of precancerous lesions, particularly in the oral cavity and larynx. These lesions may resemble harmless mucosal changes on the surface and can often only be reliably identified through a tissue biopsy.

Reliable biological markers are needed to better assess the risk. One potential marker is the protein p53, which plays a key role in controlling cell growth and the stability of genetic information.

Recent studies show that changes in p53 expression can provide clues as to whether precancerous lesions will develop into cancer or whether there is an increased risk of recurrence following a tumor.

The aim of this study is to investigate the significance of p53 expression in precancerous lesions and cancers in the head and neck region in order to improve early detection and individual risk assessment.
conditions: Dysplasia, Carcinoma, and Leukoplakia in Head and Neck Tumors

interventions.name: A retrospective analysis of all patients with dysplasia, leukoplakia, and carcinoma in the head and neck region between 2010 and 2025.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with dysplasia, leukoplakia, or carcinoma in the head and neck region
Exclusion criteria:
Patients without dysplasia, leukoplakia, or carcinoma in the head and neck region
